newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares race up at the close.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares race up at the close.

text.p: Italian shares closed well up on Monday, fuelled by Wall Street's robust opening and by speculation that shareholders in Telecom Italia could do well out of a planned merger with state telecom holding Stet.
The all-share Mibtel index finished 1.9 percent higher at 10,316 with the Mib30 index finishing 2.09 percent up at 15,398.
Firmer bond markets, boosted by agreement by EU leaders on a stability pact at a weekend summit in Dublin, also injected positive sentiment into the stock market.
Telecom Italia was the star performer, ending 5.23 percent higher at 3,622 lire while Stet finished 3.84 percent up at 6,412 lire.

Rising hopes that the Bank of France will cut official interest rates before the end of the year -- giving the Bank of Italy increasing leeway to cut its own discount rate -- was another factor fuelling the more buoyant trend.
Trading in Telecom Italia and Stet was suspended briefly pending the announcement by the Treasury that it would pay 14.53 trillion lire to take over its controlling stake in Stet fromj IRI.
Some market operators took that as a signal that Telecom shareholders would receive a favourable price for their shares when they are absorbed into Stet.
Shares in oil group ENI also powered ahead, finishing 3.14 percent higher while information technology group Olivetti also ended 3.16 percent higher at 531.8 lire.
